_note: The committed, machine-readable release policy for this application. Every field
here is READ BY release/lib/decide.mjs and therefore enforced; nothing in this
file is decoration. release/README.md explains the reasoning for a human reader
and is documentation, NOT the gate (D08-A2).
Changing any value here is an ordinary reviewed pull request, and that is the
point: the compatible set below is a thing that exists in the repository rather
than a thing somebody remembers.
The certifying workflow is resolved by PATH, through the GitHub API, and only
then compared with what the triggering event claimed. `workflow_run.workflows`
can match a workflow's mutable DISPLAY NAME and nothing else, so the name in
publish.yml is a coarse pre-filter GitHub forces on us — never the proof.
requiredChecks names the jobs inside that workflow whose success IS the
certification. A missing check is refused exactly as a failed one is.
A certification describes a moment. The evidence behind it — above all the
dependency audit (D13/B2) — does not stay true indefinitely, so a candidate
that has been sitting in an artifact for longer than this window must be
re-certified rather than promoted on an old statement.
24 hours is the operational default adopted in the Stage B approval. It is
named here rather than hidden in a script so that changing it is a decision.
THE configuration that ships. CI and the certifying run build this and nothing
else, and the publisher refuses an artifact stamped with any other name.
`uat` is the honest name for it: it carries the UAT-targeted API origin, which
is the destination this stack has today and which Stage B deliberately does NOT
change. It is not 'production' and this file does not call it that. The
environment it bakes sets Angular's `production` flag FALSE — recorded in every
manifest as environment.productionFlag so the diagnostic behaviour that follows
from it is a written-down fact rather than a discovery.
expectedApiUrl and forbiddenOriginsInBundle are asserted against the BUILT
BYTES by `release/cli.mjs stamp`, not against the source. A file replacement
that silently failed would otherwise produce an artifact that passes every
check and points at the wrong API.
The destination, pinned. identityOrigin is the canonical Firebase site origin
for this target and is where the served-release identity is read back from.
publicDirectory is the directory `firebase.json` must declare as the
hosting block's `public`. It is the field that decides WHAT gets published,
and the publisher places the verified artifact at exactly that path beside
the certified configuration — so a certified commit that moved it would
deploy a different tree, successfully, and the post-publish identity read
would notice only afterwards.
This is NOT a claim that it is the only origin serving this content: which
custom domains are mapped to this site is an owner inventory item (Stage A
WP-21), and a printed diner QR URL is a long-lived artifact whose origin and
path continuity must be planned rather than assumed. Nothing here redirects,
reroutes or reprints anything.
No release has ever published an identity file, so the first publication has
nothing to order itself against. That is a real state exactly once, and it is
an EXPLICITLY AUTHORIZED bootstrap rather than a permanent hole: while this is
false the publisher refuses a candidate it cannot place in order.
Flipping it to true is an owner decision recorded in a reviewed pull request,
and the same pull request should flip it back once an identity is being served.
The approved combination. An unchanged component is PINNED, never 'latest' —
that is what makes 'the compatible set' a thing rather than a recollection.
The peers are recorded at the commits reviewed on 22 September 2026. Their
published capability levels and the D01 ceiling digest were read from that
backend commit's source; the digest is computed over the ceiling VALUES in a
canonical form Python and JavaScript produce byte for byte, so a ceiling
changed on one side and not the other cannot be released.
THIS FILE PINS THE PEERS AND DESCRIBES THIS APPLICATION BY ITS REQUIREMENTS.
It deliberately does not pin the frontend's own commit: a repository file
cannot contain the SHA of the commit that introduces it.

admin._note: Pinned for the record. The Admin portal is a separate origin with its own publication path; nothing in this repository promotes it.

_note: Firebase Hosting retains previous releases and can re-promote one, but WHAT IS
RETAINED for this site has not been established by this repository and cannot
be from source. Until it is, a rollback whose target cannot be shown to be
retained is refused rather than attempted — `targetRetained: unknown` is not
`true`. Establishing retention is an owner action (Stage A WP-21).
The storage barrier below is separate and is NOT an owner decision: an older
bundle's reader discards a checkout record written by a newer one, dropping an
outstanding idempotency key and minting a fresh one, which is how one purchase
becomes two orders. It is enforced in decide.mjs and ships WITH the rollback
capability, never after it.
PUBLICATION IS DISABLED UNTIL AN OWNER ENABLES IT. Milestone B1 delivers the
certification and publication BOUNDARY; it performs no production cutover, and
merging it changes nothing about what is deployed or by whom. The existing
deploy-prod.yml is untouched and remains the live path.
The publisher evaluates every gate above and reports the decision it would act
on, then stops, because the repository variable named here is not set. Setting
it — and retiring deploy-prod.yml in the same change — is the cutover, and it
is its own small, reviewable pull request.
This is an enablement, not a skipped check: nothing above it is bypassed.
